title: 1999 AHSME Problem 22
statement: The graphs of \(y = -|x - a| + b\) and \(y = |x - c| + d\) intersect at points \((2, 5)\) and \((8, 3).\) Find \(a + c.\)

solutions.text:
At an intersection, \(-|x-a|+b=|x-c|+d,\) or \[|x-a|+|x-c|=b-d.\] Because there are two isolated intersections, they lie on opposite sides of the interval with endpoints \(a\) and \(c.\) The two solutions are symmetric about \(x=\tfrac{a+c}{2}.\) Their \(x\)-coordinates are \(2\) and \(8,\) so \(a+c=2+8=10.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The first graph peaks at \((a, b);\) the second bottoms out at \((c, d)\)
Rewrite the intersection equation as \(|x-a|+|x-c|=b-d\) and use symmetry
